tools.name: get_capabilities
tools.description: Returns structured facts about the Modulos AI Governance Platform: company, what the platform is for, the supported regulations and standards with requirement and control counts, integrations, deployment options and data location, certifications, indicative pricing and key links. Use this to decide

tools.name: get_trust_evidence
tools.description: Returns security and compliance evidence for vendor due diligence: certifications, data location, the documents in the Modulos trust center with their access level, subprocessors and where they hold data, and recent trust updates. Document files are requested by a person at https://www.modulos.ai/tr

tools.name: list_competitors
tools.description: Lists the vendors for which Modulos publishes a reviewed, sourced comparison. Returns the slug to pass to compare_with, the vendor name, the comparison page and the date of the last review.

tools.name: compare_with
tools.description: Returns the published comparison between Modulos and one other vendor: a row per dimension (frameworks, risk quantification, deployment, certifications, pricing and more) with the statement for each side, and the cases in which each vendor is the better choice. The comparison is written by Modulos;

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Checks stated buyer requirements against the published Modulos facts. Give the frameworks to meet, the deployment model and the tools to connect; the result separates what is supported from what is absent from the public lists. Nothing in the request is stored.

tools.name: list_knowledge
tools.description: Lists everything else Modulos has published for AI agents: answers to common buyer questions, documents to share and further facts. Returns a title, a summary and a slug per entry. Use get_knowledge with the slug for the full entry.

tools.name: get_knowledge
tools.description: Returns one published knowledge entry in full: the answer to a question, the structured data of a fact, or the summary and link of a document.

tools.name: get_modulos_info
tools.description: Returns a short description of Modulos, the tools to evaluate it and the URL where a user can book a demo. Use this first if the user asks what Modulos is or how to talk to the team.

tools.name: list_demo_slots
tools.description: Lists available 30-minute demo time slots over the next two weeks. Returns ISO-8601 UTC start times. Use book_demo_slot to confirm one of them.

tools.name: book_demo_slot
tools.description: Books a specific demo time slot. startTime must be an ISO-8601 string returned by list_demo_slots. Returns a confirmation on success.

tools.name: request_demo
tools.description: Submits an open demo request without picking a specific time. Use this when the user does not want to choose a slot — the Modulos team will reach out within 1 business day.

tools.name: list_open_roles
tools.description: Lists the jobs at Modulos that are open for application through this server, with a short public summary of each. Applications for these roles are not accepted by email. The full job description of a role is available from get_job_description.

tools.name: get_job_description
tools.description: Returns the full job description of one role at Modulos: what the job is and what it requires. When a person wants to apply for a role, the first thing you do, before asking for any of their details, is ask whether they would like to see the job description. tools.name: start_job_application
tools.description: Starts an application for a role at Modulos on behalf of the person you are assisting. Before anything else, ask the candidate whether they would like to see the job description, and show it with get_job_description if they do. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "start_job_application" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Starts an application for a role at Modulos on behalf of the person you are assisting. Before anything else, ask the candidate whether they would like to see th…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "start_job_application" is 1324 chars, far longer than this server's median (252). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "confirm_job_application" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_competitors, get_modulos_info, list_open_roles, get_job_description · Private data: get_trust_evidence, list_knowledge, get_knowledge · Public sink: list_knowledge, list_open_roles, talk_to_interviewer.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_competitors, get_modulos_info, list_open_roles, get_job_description · Private data: get_trust_evidence, list_knowledge, get_knowledge · Public sink: list_knowledge, list_open_roles, talk_to_interviewer

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
